title: Design Evolution Handbook: Component Usage, Token Migration & Deprecation Workflow
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a concise, example-driven handbook for the design system team and engineers that documents stable usage patterns for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts; defines a repeatable migration and deprecation workflow; and supplies copy-paste examples for component APIs and accessibility best practices. Scope: tokens (semantic -> platform tokens), primary/secondary button behaviour, table row density and virtualisation patterns, chart color mapping and legend semantics. This ticket is focused on authoring the handbook content, collecting code snippets, and coordinating design + engineering sign-offs. Engineering implementation tasks (component code changes) are tracked in dependent ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Handbook document published to Confluence + linked from Design System docs site
At least one example per component type (tokens/buttons/tables/charts) with do/don't and minimal runnable snippet
Migration checklist with explicit token mapping and deprecation dates included
Sign-off recorded from Platform UI eng lead and Product manager
Accessibility checklist present for each component with WCAG references
Rollout plan for documentation-only release and subsequent component deprecation windows
tasks: Draft migration mapping for semantic tokens to new platform tokens
Create 6 do/don't code examples (React + CSS tokens) for buttons and tables
Prototype lightweight chart color tokens and legend best practices in Figma
Collect runtime performance notes for table virtualization (link to ENG benchmarks)
Run design review with UX writing for copying and example captions
Publish handbook to Confluence, add link to docs site, and announce in #ds-updates
decisions: Adopt semantic tokens namespace 'ui.*' for surface tokens and 'motion.*' for transitions (agreed 2026-02-05 design sync)
Deprecation cadence: announce 90 days, followed by 180-day removal window for code tokens; component-level deprecation will follow separate ENG schedule
Buttons: primary/secondary will share base API; 'appearance' prop replaced by explicit boolean flags for 'destructive' and 'ghost' to avoid ambiguous naming
Tables: default density will be medium; compact density available as opt-in via 'density' prop; virtualization recommended for >1k rows
Charts: color tokens must map to palettes defined in tokens file; legends must use textual labels with color chips for colorblind support
migration_patterns: Phased migration: 1) provide alias tokens that map old names to new names, 2) add lint rule that warns on deprecated tokens, 3) remove aliases after deprecation window
Buttons migration: introduce 'ButtonV2' component behind feature flag; provide codemod to replace 'appearance' values with explicit props
Tables migration: wrap large-table rendering in 'VirtualizedTable' export and provide wrapper that preserves current API but swaps implementation once client upgrades
Charts migration: supply compatibility adapter that remaps legacy color keys to new palette names at render time
do_dont_examples: Button DO: <Button primary>Start</Button> with accessible label and focus-visible styles.
Button DON'T: use <button style="background: #0a0a0a"> for brand colors; avoid hard-coded hexes in components.
Table DO: use semantic column headers and <caption> for table summaries; enable 'aria-rowcount' for virtualized tables.
Table DON'T: render >2000 DOM rows without virtualization; avoid inline styles for row height that conflict with density tokens.
Chart DO: use color tokens e.g., token('chart.positive') and provide text labels for each series; include 'aria-describedby' for chart summaries.
Chart DON'T: rely solely on color or shape to convey meaning; avoid palette choices that fail contrast requirements for key labels.
api_notes: Buttons: new API replaces 'appearance: "ghost"|"primary"' with props: ghost=true, destructive=true; keep 'size' prop and normalize 'sm|md|lg' to design system scale
Tables: table props now include 'density', 'stickyHeader', and 'virtualize'; cell renderers should accept a standardized 'cellContext' object (id, rowIndex, columnKey)
Charts: color input accepts token keys or raw hex; prefer token keys and validate in dev build; series metadata should include 'label' and 'colorToken' fields
Tokens: add deprecated metadata in token JSON so docs and linting can surface specific replacement strings
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish handbook to Confluence and link in Design System docs site (docs-only release)
Week 1-4: Work with ENG to introduce compatibility aliases and lint warnings (ENG-51234)
Week 5-12: Provide codemods and address top migration blockers reported by early adopters
Week 13: Announce deprecation enforcement window start (remove aliases after 90 days notice)
Post-deprecation: Monitor adoption KPIs and open hotfixes for unexpected regressions
risk_mitigation: Provide compatibility aliases to minimize immediate breakages
Stage deprecation messages in code (console.warn) and in PR templates
Coordinate with Platform reliability team to ensure table virtualization does not regress memory SLOs (see ENG perf dashboard link)
Offer small bounty/engineering hours to teams with high migration friction
accessibility_notes: Buttons: ensure 4.5:1 contrast for primary/secondary states and 3:1 for large text per WCAG AA
Tables: include screen-reader-only summaries (<caption> + sr-only description) and ensure keyboard focus order is preserved when virtualizing rows
Charts: provide textual descriptions and data tables for complex charts; implement aria-labels for interactive legends
Tokens: provide accessible contrast helpers in the docs and show pass/fail badges for each palette token
analytics_and_kpis: Adoption rate: percentage of repositories using new token namespace within 90 days
Lint warning volume: track weekly counts of deprecated token lint warnings
Docs engagement: pageviews and average time on 'Handbook' page
Support load: number of migration-related support tickets opened in first 90 days

Detailed API changes will be delivered as follow-up ENG tickets with migration codemods. After publishing, we'll run a two-week office hours series with other product teams to surface blockers.
